key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation follows two different solid-state conversion routes in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks, and controlling those pathways enables the first fully evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a bandgap-specific process rule set for scalable, solvent-free fabrication of tandem absorbers with improved performance and thermal stability.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Compare conversion behavior in mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG absorbers
Link final bandgap to precursor-layer thickness and solid-state diffusion/reorganization
evidence_signal: The authors report bandgaps from 1.26 to 1.96 eV, 19.2% tandem efficiency, and 80% average efficiency retention after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: Vertical compositional gradients and incomplete interdiffusion in NBG stacks may complicate reproducibility and long-term uniformity at scale.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
